findings.what: OK_PREDICATE only matches `.ok === true` / `.ok !== true`, so equivalent field-only liveness predicates like `records.some(({ ok }) => ok === true)` are not flagged.
findings.why: The guard is claimed to catch a new same-session reader that trusts field-only ok:true records. A simple destructured predicate still reads dispatch-completions and gates on unsigned ok:true, but `scan()` returns zero violations, so the recurrence-stopper is incomplete.

findings.what: VERIFIES is applied to raw text and treats verifier names inside comments as proof of verification.
findings.why: A new unverified reader with `// TODO route this through isVerifiedLivenessRecord later` within the +/-12-line window passes with zero violations. That recreates the per-read token-hollow problem: a verifier token near the read, without a verifier call, suppresses the structural guard.

parsed.summary: Current converted readers in the scoped files route their ok:true liveness reads through isVerifiedLivenessRecord/verifyRecord, and the three liveness-verified pragmas are genuine shape-only/reject-only/non-ledger cases. The guard also catches the canonical unverified `r.ok === true` case in all of scripts/. However, it still fails to catch simple equivalent same-session readers and comment-only verifier tokens, so the same-session reader consolidation is not complete.
